overview: Hepatitis D is an inflammation of the liver caused by the hepatitis D virus (HDV), which requires hepatitis B virus (HBV) for its replication. HDV–HBV co-infection is considered the most severe form of chronic viral hepatitis due to more rapid progression towards hepatocellular carcinoma and liver-related death. Vaccination against hepatitis B can prevent HDV infection.
diagnosis: molecular methods to demonstrate the presence of HDV RNA
treatment: nucleoside analogues for managing chronic HBV infection
combination therapy with PEG-IFNα and other agents
transmission: vertical transmission from mother to child
transmission within families in endemic areas
prevention: antiviral prophylaxis for eligible pregnant women
harm reduction services with clean needles and syringes
risk_factors: people with hepatitis C virus or HIV infection
men who have sex with men
key_facts: HDV affects nearly 5% of people globally who have a chronic infection with HBV
HDV has recently been classified as carcinogenic to humans
vaccination against hepatitis B can prevent HDV infection
